rows.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
rows.stem: With increase in atomic number, the melting point of transition metals :
rows.solution:
The melting point FIRST INCREASES AND THEN DECREASES across a transition series.

Melting a metal means overcoming its metallic bonding, and the strength of that bonding tracks the number of UNPAIRED d electrons available to take part in it, alongside the \(ns\) electrons.

Going across the series the unpaired electrons increase to a maximum near the middle and then decrease again as pairing begins. The melting points follow: scandium melts at about 1814 K, chromium — with six unpaired electrons, the most of any element in the first series — reaches about 2130 K, and by zinc, whose \(3d\) subshell is completely filled and contributes nothing at all, the figure has collapsed to 693 K.

Manganese is the one dip in the rising half, its unusual crystal structure weakening the bonding there.

rows.subtopic: Colligative Properties and Determination of Molar Mass
rows.stem: Which of the following aqueous solutions will have the highest osmotic pressure ?
rows.solution:
The highest osmotic pressure belongs to the 1% CALCIUM CHLORIDE solution.

Osmotic pressure is a colligative property, \(\Pi = CRT\), so it depends on the NUMBER OF PARTICLES in solution and not on what they are. Each solution here holds 1 g of solute, so compare moles of particles per gram.

Calcium chloride dissociates into THREE ions from a molar mass of 111, giving \(3/111 = 0{\cdot}027\). Potassium chloride gives two ions from 74.5, so \(2/74{\cdot}5 = 0{\cdot}0268\) — very close, but just behind. Urea gives \(1/60 = 0{\cdot}0167\) and glucose only \(1/180 = 0{\cdot}0056\).

The two non-electrolytes are easily eliminated; the real contest is between the two salts, and calcium chloride wins on the extra ion.

rows.stem: A conductivity cell usually consists of two :
rows.solution:
A conductivity cell uses two PLATINUM electrodes, usually coated with platinum black.

Platinum is chosen because it is chemically INERT: it neither dissolves in the solution being measured nor reacts with it, so the composition stays what it was. Copper, zinc and iron would all take part in the chemistry and corrupt the reading.

The platinum black coating serves a second purpose — it enormously increases the effective surface area of the electrodes, which suppresses the polarisation that would otherwise build up at their surfaces.

The two plates are fixed a set distance apart, and the ratio of that separation to their area is the cell constant, which converts the measured resistance into conductivity.

rows.stem: Which of the following is the slope of the first order reaction in the plot of \(\ln [\mathrm{R}]\) vs. time ?
rows.solution:
The slope is \(-k\).

For a first order reaction, integrating the rate law gives
\(\ln[\mathrm{R}] = \ln[\mathrm{R}]_0 - kt\)

Compare with \(y = c + mx\), taking \(y\) as \(\ln[\mathrm{R}]\) and \(x\) as \(t\): the intercept is \(\ln[\mathrm{R}]_0\) and the slope is \(-k\).

The slope is NEGATIVE because the reactant is being consumed, so the line falls; and the rate constant is recovered as \(k = -\text{slope}\).

The factor of 2.303 in two of the options belongs to the version of the same equation written with common logarithms, \(\log[\mathrm{R}]\), where the slope is \(-k/2{\cdot}303\). Here the plot uses the NATURAL logarithm, so no conversion factor appears.

rows.stem: The number of moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) precipitated when excess \(\mathrm{AgNO_3}\) solution is mixed with one mole of \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3}\) is :
rows.solution:
THREE moles of silver chloride are precipitated.

Silver nitrate precipitates only the chloride that is FREE IN SOLUTION, that is the counter ions outside the coordination sphere. In \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3}\) the square brackets enclose cobalt and its six ammonia ligands, and nothing else: all three chlorides sit OUTSIDE, as counter ions, and every one of them ionises.

Check the charges: six ammonia molecules are neutral, so with cobalt at \(+3\) the complex ion is \(+3\) — balanced by exactly three chlorides outside.

\(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]Cl_3} \longrightarrow \mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}} + 3\mathrm{Cl^-}\)

What is precipitated counts what is outside the brackets, never the total chlorine. Moving one chloride inside, as in \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_5Cl]Cl_2}\), would drop the count to 2.

rows.stem: Which of the following haloalkanes is most reactive towards \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) reaction ?
rows.solution:
IODOETHANE, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2I}\), is the most reactive towards the bimolecular route.

All four have the same carbon skeleton, so steric hindrance is identical and the only variable is the HALOGEN — specifically how good a leaving group it makes. The \(\mathrm{C-X}\) bond must break as the nucleophile attacks, so the weaker that bond, the faster the reaction.

Bond strength falls steadily down the group as the halogen gets larger and its orbital overlaps less well with carbon's: \(\mathrm{C-F}\) is much the strongest, then \(\mathrm{C-Cl}\), \(\mathrm{C-Br}\), \(\mathrm{C-I}\) the weakest. The iodide ion is also the most stable of the four anions, being the largest and best able to spread its charge.

So reactivity runs iodide, bromide, chloride, fluoride — and the fluoride is so unreactive that it is hardly ever used for substitution at all.

rows.stem:
The reaction
\(\mathrm{C_6H_5-OH} + \mathrm{NaOH\,(aq)} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5-O^{-}Na^{+}} + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{H_2\,(g)}\)
suggests that phenol is :
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE — both phenol and the phenoxide are printed as DRAWN benzene rings rather than formulas, read here losslessly as \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-OH}\) and \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-O^{-}Na^{+}}\). NAMED, not described: the question asks what the reaction shows about phenol's acid-base character, so reading the rings as formulas cannot state the answer. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
The reaction shows that phenol is ACIDIC.

Sodium hydroxide is a base, and phenol reacts with it to give a SALT, sodium phenoxide. Only an acid does that — what leaves the phenol is the hydrogen of its hydroxyl group as \(\mathrm{H^+}\), and the phenoxide ion left behind is the conjugate base.

Phenol is a far stronger acid than an alcohol, with \(\mathrm{pK_a}\) about 10 against about 16, because the phenoxide ion's negative charge is delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance while an alkoxide's is stuck on one oxygen. That difference is itself a standard test: phenol dissolves in sodium hydroxide, ethanol does not.

One point on the equation as printed. Sodium HYDROXIDE gives the salt and WATER, not hydrogen:
\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH} + \mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5O^-Na^+} + \mathrm{H_2O}\)
Hydrogen is evolved when the reagent is sodium METAL:
\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH} + \mathrm{Na} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5O^-Na^+} + \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{H_2}\)
Either reaction demonstrates the same thing, so the conclusion is unaffected.

rows.stem: Phenol reacts with conc. \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) to form :
rows.solution:
Phenol with concentrated nitric acid gives PICRIC ACID, that is 2,4,6-trinitrophenol.

The hydroxyl group is strongly activating — its lone pair is fed into the ring, raising the electron density most at the ortho and para positions — so all three of those positions are nitrated:
\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. }\mathrm{HNO_3}} \mathrm{C_6H_2(NO_2)_3OH}\)

The product is a yellow solid and a genuinely strong acid, far stronger than phenol itself, because three nitro groups pull electron density away and stabilise the anion.

DILUTE nitric acid is the contrast: it stops at the mono-substituted stage and gives a mixture of 2-nitrophenol and 4-nitrophenol.

rows.stem: Anilinium hydrogen sulphate on heating at 453 – 473 K produces which of the following as a major product ?
rows.solution:
The major product is SULPHANILIC ACID, that is 4-aminobenzenesulphonic acid.

Aniline with sulphuric acid first gives the salt, anilinium hydrogen sulphate. Heating that salt to 453-473 K rearranges it so the sulphonic acid group ends up ON THE RING, and at the PARA position — the site the amino group activates and the one least crowded:
\(\mathrm{C_6H_5\overset{+}{N}H_3\,HSO_4^{-}} \xrightarrow{453\text{-}473\ \mathrm{K}} \mathrm{p\text{-}H_2N{-}C_6H_4{-}SO_3H}\)

Sulphanilic acid exists almost entirely as its ZWITTER ION, the amino group having taken the sulphonic acid's proton — which is why it melts so high and dissolves so poorly in organic solvents.

The ortho isomer offered as a distractor is the minor product; benzenesulphonic acid would require the amino group to be lost altogether.

rows.stem: Which of the following amines does **not** give foul smell of isocyanide on heating with chloroform and ethanolic KOH ?
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE — option (D) is printed as a DRAWN benzene ring bearing \(\mathrm{NH_2}\), read here losslessly as \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-NH_2}\) (aniline); option (B) prints its \(\mathrm{CH_3}\) branch on a VERTICAL bond below the second carbon and is written inline here as \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-NH_2}\), the same connectivity. NAMED, not described: the answer is the tertiary amine (C), so reading (B) and (D) losslessly cannot state it. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
TRIETHYLAMINE, \(\mathrm{(CH_3CH_2)_3N}\), gives no isocyanide.

This is the CARBYLAMINE test, and it detects PRIMARY amines only. Chloroform with alcoholic potassium hydroxide generates dichlorocarbene, and forming an isocyanide requires the nitrogen to give up BOTH of its hydrogens to the carbon:
\(\mathrm{R{-}NH_2} + \mathrm{CHCl_3} + 3\mathrm{KOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{R{-}NC} + 3\mathrm{KCl} + 3\mathrm{H_2O}\)

A tertiary amine has NO hydrogen on its nitrogen at all, so the reaction cannot even begin.

The other three all qualify. Ethylamine and 2-methylpropan-1-amine are primary aliphatic amines, and aniline is a primary aromatic one — the test works for both kinds, which is why the foul smell is such a reliable indicator of a primary amine. A secondary amine, had one been offered, would also have failed, having only one hydrogen where two are needed.

rows.stem: Deficiency of vitamin \(\mathrm{B_1}\) causes the disease :

options.label: C
options.text: Fissuring at corners of mouth and lips (Cheilosis)

rows.solution:
A deficiency of vitamin \(\mathrm{B_1}\), thiamine, causes BERI-BERI.

Thiamine is needed for carbohydrate metabolism, so without it the nerves and the heart muscle suffer: beri-beri shows as loss of appetite, weakness and wasting, with nerve damage or heart failure in its severe forms. It is WATER SOLUBLE, so the body cannot store a reserve and a regular dietary supply is needed.

Of the others offered: convulsions come from a deficiency of vitamin \(\mathrm{B_6}\), cheilosis from vitamin \(\mathrm{B_2}\), and muscular weakness from vitamin E.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : A mixture of \(o\)-nitrophenol and \(p\)-nitrophenol can be separated by fractional distillation.
Reason (R) : \(o\)-nitrophenol is steam volatile due to intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The Assertion is FALSE while the Reason is TRUE.

The two nitrophenols CAN be separated, and the Reason correctly explains why — o-nitrophenol is steam volatile because its nitro and hydroxyl groups hydrogen bond to each other WITHIN the same molecule, so its molecules do not associate with one another. That is genuine, and it is the whole basis of the separation.

But the Assertion names the WRONG TECHNIQUE. The method is STEAM distillation, not FRACTIONAL distillation. Fractional distillation separates liquids by repeated vaporisation and condensation up a column and would be useless here, since both compounds are solids at room temperature with high and close boiling points.

Steam distillation is a different operation altogether: steam is passed through the mixture and carries the volatile component over with it at a temperature below the boiling point of either, leaving the associated p-nitrophenol behind.

This is the sibling of a question whose Assertion says "steam distillation" — there the whole statement is true. One word changes the answer.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water than in warm water.
Reason (R) : Solubility of oxygen gas in water decreases with increase in temperature.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Both statements are true and the Reason IS the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Dissolving a gas in a liquid is an EXOTHERMIC process, so by Le Chatelier's principle raising the temperature drives it backwards: the solubility of oxygen in water FALLS as the water warms.

Aquatic species breathe the oxygen dissolved in the water around them, so warm water simply offers them less of it. That is exactly why cold water suits them better, and the Reason therefore accounts for the Assertion completely.

The practical consequence is thermal pollution: warm water discharged from a power station into a river threatens the fish in it without adding anything toxic at all.

rows.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : First ionisation enthalpy of Cr is lower than that of Zn.
Reason (R) : Zinc is a non-transition element.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Both statements are true, but the Reason is NOT the correct explanation of the Assertion.

The first ionisation enthalpy of chromium IS lower than that of zinc — about 653 against 906 kJ per mole — and zinc IS a non-transition element, having a completely filled \(3d\) subshell both as the atom and in its \(+2\) ion.

But the second fact does not cause the first. The difference in ionisation enthalpy comes from which electron is being removed and how it is held. Chromium is \(3d^5 4s^1\), with a single, loosely held \(4s\) electron whose removal leaves the stable half-filled \(3d^5\) behind. Zinc is \(3d^{10}4s^2\), with a filled \(4s\) orbital shielded by a completed d subshell, so its electron is held much more tightly and removing it breaks up a stable arrangement rather than producing one.

Zinc's classification follows from the same full d subshell, so the two statements share a cause — but neither is the reason for the other.

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Vitamin C cannot be stored in our body.
Reason (R) : Vitamin C is water soluble and excreted in urine.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Both statements are true and the Reason IS the correct explanation of the Assertion.

Vitamin C, ascorbic acid, is WATER SOLUBLE. Any excess taken in dissolves in the body's aqueous fluids and passes straight out in the urine rather than being laid down anywhere — so no reserve accumulates, and a regular dietary supply is required. That is precisely why it cannot be stored, and the Reason explains the Assertion completely.

The contrast is with the FAT-soluble vitamins — A, D, E and K — which are stored in the liver and in adipose tissue, and which therefore need not be supplied daily.

The practical consequence is historical: scurvy, the disease of vitamin C deficiency, appeared on long sea voyages after only a few weeks without fresh food.

rows.stem:
(a) A and B liquids on mixing show rise in temperature. Which type of deviation from Raoult’s law is there and why ?
(b) Why can azeotropic mixture not be separated by fractional distillation ?
rows.solution:
(a) A rise in temperature on mixing means the process is EXOTHERMIC — energy is being released — and that identifies a NEGATIVE DEVIATION from Raoult's law.

Energy is released when new interactions form that are stronger than the ones broken. So the attraction between UNLIKE molecules, A with B, must be STRONGER than the attractions between like molecules, A with A and B with B.

Held more tightly, the molecules escape into the vapour less readily than Raoult's law predicts, so the vapour pressure of the solution is LOWER than the ideal value. The volume also contracts slightly on mixing — the same fact seen a third way.

(b) Because an azeotrope has the SAME COMPOSITION IN THE LIQUID AND IN THE VAPOUR PHASE.

Fractional distillation works by exploiting a difference between the two: the vapour is always richer in the more volatile component, so each condensation and re-vaporisation up the column enriches it further.

At the azeotropic composition that difference vanishes. The vapour that comes off is identical to the liquid it came from, so no number of stages changes anything — the mixture distils over unaltered, as though it were a pure compound.

rows.subtopic: Factors Influencing Rate of a Reaction
rows.stem: Why is molecularity applicable only for elementary reactions and order is applicable for elementary as well as complex reactions ?
rows.solution:
The difference is that MOLECULARITY describes a SINGLE STEP while ORDER describes the OVERALL reaction as it is observed.

WHY MOLECULARITY IS RESTRICTED. Molecularity counts the number of species that must COLLIDE for a reaction to occur — so it presupposes that there is one collision to count. An elementary reaction takes place in a single step, and the count is unambiguous.

A complex reaction is a SEQUENCE of elementary steps, and each step may have a different molecularity — one unimolecular, the next bimolecular, and so on. There is no single number to assign to the sequence, so molecularity is meaningless for the reaction as a whole.

WHY ORDER IS NOT RESTRICTED. Order is determined EXPERIMENTALLY, from how the measured rate responds when concentrations are changed. That measurement can be made on any reaction whatever, however many steps it takes — for a complex reaction the observed order is governed by the SLOWEST step, the rate determining one.

Two consequences follow. Order may be zero or fractional, because it is measured; molecularity must be a whole number of at least 1, because it counts colliding species. And for an elementary reaction alone the two coincide, since there the one step IS the reaction.

rows.stem: Write two differences between DNA and RNA.
rows.solution:
STRAND AND SUGAR. DNA is DOUBLE stranded — two chains wound into a helix and held together by hydrogen bonds between complementary bases — and its sugar is \(\beta\)-D-2-DEOXYRIBOSE, which lacks the hydroxyl group at \(\mathrm{C_2}\). RNA is SINGLE stranded, and its sugar is \(\beta\)-D-RIBOSE, with that hydroxyl group present.

BASES AND FUNCTION. Both carry adenine, guanine and cytosine, but the fourth base differs: DNA has THYMINE where RNA has URACIL. And DNA REPLICATES, carrying the genetic information from one generation to the next, whereas RNA does not replicate — it is synthesised from DNA and directs the synthesis of proteins.

The missing hydroxyl group is what makes the difference in stability: DNA is the more chemically durable of the two, which suits the molecule that has to store information permanently.
